definition: Deciding per input which of several processing paths to take, rather than applying one procedure uniformly. One source routes on a text-only regex detector of restrictive cues, activating a two-stage constraint-extraction protocol only where constraints exist to exploit and falling back to direct chain-of-thought otherwise. The other routes at every generation step among a fast path, a slow perception path and a slow reasoning path, with the router trained by multi-objective RL on roughly 790k samples of teacher-attributed perception-versus-reasoning failures. The pair spans the design range: a hand-written detector applied once per problem, and a learned controller applied at each step.

evidence.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
evidence.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

evidence.note: Routes each generation step among a fast path, a perception re-examination path and a self-reflection path, trained on 790k samples of teacher-attributed perception-versus-reasoning failures.
evidence.title: Addressing Overthinking in Large Vision-Language Models via Gated Perception-Reasoning Optimization

name: routing
